title: Compliance Reporting Pack (Baseline) — Customer Brief (AE/SE slides draft)
content:
Slide 1 — Title
Compliance Reporting Pack (Baseline)
Customer brief for enterprise security reviews

Speaker notes:
Use this when a customer asks for “proof of retention + audit logging” or wants a standardized evidence bundle for SOC 2 / ISO-style reviews. This is not a SOC 2 report replacement; it’s a Redwood-produced evidence package.


Slide 2 — Why this exists (what customers are asking for)
- Security questionnaires repeatedly block on: retention, audit logs, access controls, and data residency
- Customers want: a repeatable package (not a bespoke scramble every deal)
- Internal goal: reduce AE/SE + Security time spent on one-off evidence pulls

Speaker notes:
Position this as a predictable process + artifact set. We can still answer edge cases, but this covers 80–90% of review requests.


Slide 3 — What is the “Baseline Compliance Reporting Pack”
A customer-ready bundle that includes:
- Retention configuration export (by data class) + change history excerpt
- Audit-log coverage summary + sample exports (time-windowed)
- Data residency / region summary (where workloads + telemetry are processed/stored by tier)
- Access control / RBAC report (roles, scopes, and admin actions captured)
- Evidence collection checklist (what’s included + what’s available on request)

Speaker notes:
Use the phrase “baseline pack” consistently. Avoid calling it “attestation.” It’s an evidence package generated from our systems + documentation.


Slide 4 — What’s included (details)
1) Retention configuration export
- Data classes covered: request/response logs (where enabled), audit logs, traces/metrics (telemetry), artifacts (where applicable)
- Shows effective TTL, purge semantics, exceptions/holds, and tier defaults
- Includes policy version and last modified timestamp

2) Audit-log coverage summary
- Event categories (examples): auth/login, API key lifecycle, retention policy changes, RBAC/admin actions, export actions
- Notes known limitations (if any) and planned additions

Speaker notes:
Keep it simple: show the categories and confirm we can provide exports for a specific time window and filters.


Slide 5 — Output formats + what the customer receives
Standard deliverables (MVP):
- ZIP bundle containing:
  - JSON exports (retention config, audit logs)
  - CSV views for common audit report templates (optional per request)
  - “Customer README” explaining sections + how to interpret
  - Evidence checklist (PDF or doc)
- Delivery via secure link (customer’s preferred channel) or customer portal (where available)

Speaker notes:
If the customer needs a specific format (e.g., GRC upload), commit to exportable formats first. Don’t promise custom integrations in v1.


Slide 6 — What this pack is NOT (set expectations early)
- Not a SOC 2 / ISO certificate or third-party audit report
- Not a full custom report builder
- Not a replacement for the customer’s own control testing
- Not a guarantee that customer-configured settings are optimal (we show what’s configured + how it’s enforced)

Speaker notes:
This slide prevents the “can you fill out our entire GRC portal?” ask. We can help, but baseline pack has a defined scope.


Slide 7 — Typical timeline (what to tell customers)
Standard:
- 5 business days from request intake to delivery
Expedited (deal-critical, approved):
- 2 business days (best effort; depends on requested time window + complexity)
Customer factors that change timeline:
- Need for a specific historical window (e.g., 12 months)
- Private deployment: availability of exporter endpoints / customer-controlled environment
- Requests for additional screenshots or bespoke narrative mapping

Speaker notes:
Anchor on 5 business days. Use expedited sparingly, with clear gating (Security/GRC sign-off).


Slide 8 — How to request (internal process for AE/SE)
1) Create a request ticket (preferred):
- “Compliance Pack Request” in the GTM intake queue (Sales Ops / Support routing)
2) Provide minimum required inputs:
- Customer name + opportunity link
- Deployment tier (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Desired time window for audit export (start/end dates + timezone)
- Any event filters (actors, event types) requested by the customer
- Due date + whether expedited is requested
3) Notify:
- #gtm-compliance-pack (Slack) for visibility + scheduling

Speaker notes:
If you don’t know the time window, ask: “What period does your auditor require?” Default suggestion: last 30–90 days.


Slide 9 — Minimum inputs checklist (copy/paste for AEs)
Copy/paste:
- Customer + domain:
- Tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private):
- Regions in scope (if known):
- Audit export window (UTC preferred):
- Event categories requested (if provided):
- Retention settings questions from the questionnaire (paste):
- Delivery contact + secure delivery preference:
- Due date + procurement milestone:

Speaker notes:
This reduces back-and-forth with GRC/Security. It also helps avoid “we pulled the wrong window” issues.


Slide 10 — Tier notes (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Hosted API
- Redwood-managed control plane and telemetry stores
- Fastest turnaround for exports

Dedicated
- Dedicated capacity + isolation; reporting still from Redwood systems
- May include additional region/capacity context per customer

Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Some artifacts generated from customer-controlled environment
- May require customer admin to run exporter or grant access
- Timeline can vary based on install version + connectivity

Speaker notes:
Avoid overpromising uniformity for Private. Emphasize “consistent schema and template,” but acknowledge environment differences.


Slide 11 — Common customer questions (recommended talk track)
Q: “Do you store prompts/completions?”
- A: Depends on logging settings and tier; retention controls govern any stored request/response logs. We can export the configured policy and explain defaults.

Q: “Can you delete everything immediately?”
- A: We support retention TTLs and purge semantics; ultra-short TTLs may have operational caveats. Legal hold and incident exceptions are documented and audited.

Q: “Do you have audit logs for admin actions?”
- A: Yes; the pack includes audit-log coverage summary and a time-windowed export.

Q: “Can you map this to SOC 2 controls?”
- A: The evidence checklist is aligned to SOC 2 / ISO-style expectations, but it’s not a formal attestation.

Speaker notes:
Stay on-message: configurable retention + auditable change history + exportable evidence.


Slide 12 — Escalation + approvals (internal)
When to pull in Security/GRC:
- Customer requests contractual language about retention/holds
- Customer demands a “certification” or custom audit opinion
- Customer wants deviations from standard retention minimums/maximums
- Customer asks for additional event types not yet in exporter templates

Owners:
- Pack owner (GRC): Olga Petrov
- Security sign-off: Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin
- Export/engineering: Kevin Osei

Speaker notes:
Keep approvals tight. Don’t stall deals unnecessarily, but don’t ad-lib on legal hold or retention guarantees.


Slide 13 — What good looks like (success criteria)
- Customer can complete security review with fewer follow-ups
- Pack delivered in < 5 business days for standard requests
- Reduced ad-hoc pulls by Security/Engineering
- Consistent, repeatable evidence across deals

Speaker notes:
If asked, cite that this is part of our Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation rollout.


Slide 14 — Appendix: “One-liner” you can paste in email
“We can provide a baseline compliance reporting pack that includes (1) your effective retention configuration export (by data class), (2) an audit-log coverage summary and time-windowed audit exports, (3) data residency/region summary, (4) RBAC/access control report, and (5) an evidence checklist aligned to SOC 2/ISO-style reviews. Standard turnaround is ~5 business days once we confirm the requested time window and deployment tier.”

Speaker notes:
Use this to reply to procurement/security questionnaires. Keep it factual and avoid commitments outside the baseline scope.
